environment: **Organization**: Mozilla; web standards work in WHATWG, W3C, and wpt
**Repository visibility**: PUBLIC — repos are generally public on github.com
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: public paste/gist services are outside the trust boundary
**Default / protected branches**: `main` in upstream (non-zcorpan) repos is shared: work on a branch and open a PR, never push directly
**Host containment**: ordinary developer machine with open internet

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and never share
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development — web platform spec/test work (wpt, WHATWG spec repos, browser bug tracking)

**Trusted repos**: any public github.com repo checked out under ~/git/<org>/<repo>; repos under ~/git/zcorpan/ (and zcorpan/.claude at ~/.claude) are my own, the rest are upstreams. Since all are public, secrets/sensitive data like `.credentials.json` are never cleared into any of them
